text:
Maria N: Found a partner S3 logs bucket with a plaintext GCP service account key in /ingest/partnerX/2026-03-23/log.json. Need immediate rotation and containment. Relevant SA: redwood-ingest@project. Any advice on order of ops? cc @Akshay @Ben J
Akshay: Copy. Prioritize: 1) disable the exposed key, 2) revoke active tokens, 3) rotate any Vault references and rewrap KMS artifacts, 4) enable/confirm audit logging for Vault + KMS. I'll start the key disable. Where exactly did you find the blob?
Maria N: S3 path: s3://partner-logs-prod/ingest/partnerX/2026-03-23/xyz.log. It's a base64 JSON with a `private_key` field.
Ben J: If it's a GCP SA key, create a new SA with least-priv and update consumers. Consider switching partner ingest to a short-lived WIF or workload identity where possible. Platform Team: can we accept KMS-wrapped credentials instead of raw SA keys?
Jamie P: Platform can add KMS encryption-at-rest + signed ingest tokens. Short-term: can we add an IAM deny on KMS to prevent that SA from calling CryptoKeyVersions:Access? Also pull Cloud Audit Logs for any recent unwrap calls.
Akshay: I'll revoke now. Steps I'm running: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable KEY_ID --iam-account=redwood-ingest@project` then after verifying no active uses `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete KEY_ID --iam-account=redwood-ingest@project`. Also will list permissions: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy project-id` to see who had the SA role.
Maria N: Confirmed vault reference at `secret/data/partners/partnerx/sa-creds` — looks like plaintext JSON stored.
Ben J: Run `vault kv get -format=json secret/partners/partnerx/sa-creds | jq .data.data` to confirm. If plaintext, mark it RotateNow. We'll need an automated job to update all deploys and CI variables.
Jamie P: I'll prepare a temporary RBAC change to block CI runners from reading that vault path until rotation is done. Also request @sre-bot to create an alert for anomalous reads on that path.
sre-bot: Created alert `vault.read.anomaly.partnerx` -> webhook to #incidents.
Maria N: Thanks. Akshay, can you post deletion confirmation and key fingerprint so I can notify Partner CS/legal?
Akshay: Disabled key KEY_ID at 2026-03-23T14:12:03Z. Fingerprint SHA256:ABCDEF1234567890. Deleting now...
Akshay: Deleted KEY_ID. GCP console shows no active keys. Created new SA `redwood-ingest-temp@project` with minimal perms and generated new key. I wrapped the new key with our KMS key and stored as `secret/partners/partnerx/sa-creds-v2`.
Ben J: I'll update CI and Ansible vars to point to `sa-creds-v2`. Also kicking off a repo search for the old SA email: `git grep -n "redwood-ingest@project" || true` and a logs scan.
Maria N: I queried BigQuery audit logs; found two accesses from partner IP ranges at 2026-03-22T23:xx and 2026-03-23T01:xx — both pre-disable. No signs of data exfil currently. I'll share query results in the incident doc.
Jamie P: If Vault isn't already audited to central SIEM, enable file audit and forward: `vault audit enable file file_path=/var/log/vault_audit.log` then ship to our ELK/SIEM. Also enable KMS audit logs and set retention for investigation.
Akshay: Kicked off a rewrap job to re-encrypt old backups where the old SA key was used; setting TTLs and rotating tokens. Removing broad access grants that had the SA.
Ben J: Proposed rotation plan: 1) Notify stakeholders 2) Rotate vault secret -> deploy updates -> monitor 24h 3) Revoke any residual tokens -> sweep logs -> close. I'll open PR for automation scripts that update secrets and run smoke tests.
Maria N: Can Eng-Sec + Platform own the postmortem? We need timeline, root cause (why raw key ended up in partner logs), impacted customers, and remediation steps.
Akshay: I'll own the immediate postmortem doc and lead root cause collection. Adding @Jamie to own platform remediation.
Jamie P: On it. I'll add the runbook with commands we ran and a follow-up action to require KMS-wrapped artifacts for partner ingest by policy.
Maria N: Partner notified, CS looped, legal on standby. Leaving thread open for any anomalous re-reads or downstream failures. :white_check_mark:
